title: A walk that changes a remembered setting puts it back
goal: Two of the scripted walks only pass the first time they are ever run on a machine. One of them changes the text size from 24 to 48 and the app remembers that, so the next run looks for a 24 that is no longer there and stops. Anyone who runs the walks twice sees a failure that is not a real one, which makes the whole set less trustworthy to read.
notes: Found while regression-testing the colour picker walk work on 2026-09-04. type-menu-labels-walk step 17 is panelMenu {menu: 24 pt, choose: 48 pt}; the text size is remembered in the probe defaults, so on a second run the button reads 48 pt and the step fails with "no menu called 24 pt". drop-lands-here-walk has the same shape of problem from the other side: it carries a seed note saying to copy Scripts/playtest/fixtures/Photonz drop probe.png into ~/Pictures/Screenshots first, which nothing enforces, so it fails with "no tile called Photonz drop probe" unless a person read the note. Options: a reset step at the top of a walk, a walk-level setup block the runner performs, or the probe starting from clean defaults each launch.
acceptance: Running type-menu-labels-walk twice in a row passes both times
Running the whole walk set twice in a row produces the same result both times
Any walk that needs something set up first says so in a way the runner can act on, rather than only in a note for a person

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Three ways out were on the table: a reset step inside a walk, a setup block the runner performs, and the probe starting clean every launch. Clean every launch is wrong: the probe keeping its settings is what makes it the same app a person uses, and two walks (open-groups-remembered, open-groups-reopened) exist precisely to prove something is remembered. A reset STEP is wrong too, because it can only run after the window is already open, and the text size a new label is made in is read before that. So: a setup block, performed before step one.

Second finding, which changed the shape of the fix. type-menu-labels named the size menu "24 pt", which is its VALUE. The harness already has a rule against that for every other control (a control's name holds still; what changes about it goes in its detail), and menus were the one place it was not honoured. FrameInspector even carries a comment saying its menu is opened by the size it is showing. So a menu is now named by the row it sits on (Size, Vertical) with the value in the detail, and a panel step reads them "Size (24 pt)". Forgetting the setting alone would have left the walk fragile the moment anything else changed a size.

Built: PlaytestSetup in PhotonzCore (forget + captures, decoded with readable errors, 8 new tests); PlaytestSetupRunner in the probe performs it before step one and gives borrowed capture files back however the run ends; PlaytestPanelMenu.naming resolves a menu by its row; SelectionMenu and the Across/Down captions in TextInspector name their rows; Scripts/playtest-all.sh runs the whole folder; PlaytestWalkSetupTests holds every walk to the rule.

The static test found a third case at once: text-fills-height-walk opened "Top", chose "Stretch", then opened "Stretch". Both steps now say "Vertical". Running the panel walks found a fourth and fifth: picker-controls-walk and panel-controls-walk each draw a rectangle and open its Fill colour, which does not exist when the shape tool was last left holding no fill. Both now forget shapes and color first, and both pass.

Ran the 55 state-sensitive walks (every walk with a press, panelMenu, panel, measureMode, dragTile or a Library/measure/style action) twice back to back with Scripts/playtest-all.sh. Pass 1: 53 of 55. Pass 2: 54 of 55. The one difference between the passes was picker-controls-walk, which is a timing flake: it waits 0.8s for the colour picker to appear after pressing the Fill swatch, which is not always enough while a second run is loading the machine. That wait is now 2.0s.

The walk that failed BOTH passes, identically, was a sixth instance of this bug and the run is how it was found. label-grows-walk types a label and then drags its right edge at a fixed point; the label's size comes from the remembered text style, so once anything had left the size at 48 the handle was not where the walk reached and the drag deselected instead of resizing, and the failure only showed six steps later as "no field labelled W". It now forgets text first. The failing before/passing after was checked on the real probe, not reasoned about.

Verified: label-grows, picker-controls, type-menu-labels and drop-lands-here each run twice in a row and pass all four times, with the probe rebuilt from the final source. text-fills-height and panel-reach still pass with the new menu naming. Scripts/test.sh green (3013 tests).

Not verified: the other 77 walks in the folder were not double-run in this session. Two passes over all 132 is about three and a half hours of machine time and the user is playtesting on the same machine. Scripts/playtest-all.sh runs the whole folder for whoever wants that; the 55 chosen here are the ones that can read or write a remembered setting, which is the whole risk surface for this bug.
